solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Led army, moving to protect king — obviously

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other
moving signals the letters of the words before it are shifted into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A general led his troops on the march to guard the monarch, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns LEDARMY into MAREDLY; 'to protect' then wraps those letters round K.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in a clearly noticeable, evident way; synonyms.

clue.text: Medical Officer's son's plant

parts.note: MO is the standard abbreviation for Medical Officer, with the possessive S kept
S is the usual abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A doctor's boy has a plant of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small flowerless green plant growing in damp places; an example of the category.

clue.text: Make further changes in study, suitable

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, as at university
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Revising a study to make it suitable needs more tweaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust again for new conditions is to make further changes; a close paraphrase.

clue.text: Nice article set off sparks

indicators.note: set off suggests something triggered and sent flying, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A pleasant newspaper piece causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks' looks like a verb with 'set off'; it is the old nickname for a wiring tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is a long-standing British slang nickname for an electrical worker, as Chippy is for a carpenter.

clue.text: Folk tradition about a hot Asian city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tradition is placed round the other letters

parts.note: lore is the body of traditional folk knowledge
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Folk customs grow up around a sweltering city in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province; an example of the category.

clue.text: Feature of faith, a lovely circle?

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ring of light is part of the imagery of a beautiful faith.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a ring of light drawn round a saint's head, so a kind of circle.

clue.text: First of all ask maestro about the Italian violin

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Ask the conductor about the Italian fiddle, to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made famous fine instruments, so the name stands for one of them.

clue.text: A dry iron — sadly commonplace

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ironing without steam is a dull, everyday chore, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean usual and unremarkable; synonyms.

clue.text: A lot of similar things? Exactly right in southeast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
pat means exactly right, as in having an answer off pat

explanation.surface: Seems to be a query about matching items being exactly right in the southeast of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush of many similar events in quick succession, as in a spate of burglaries.

clue.text: Rider's careworn

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ... was the Victorian novelist who wrote King Solomon's Mines; his surname is the Rider's
careworn means looking exhausted and drawn

explanation.surface: A horseman looks tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means gaunt and drawn from worry, the same as careworn; and the novelist was H. Rider Haggard.

clue.text: Somewhat outstanding raven, I'm a general object of worship?

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A talking bird announces it is a general and is worshipped for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved idol, as forbidden in the Ten Commandments, is something worshipped.

clue.text: Lace into rat involved in quarrel

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Laying into a rodent leads to a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a noisy argument or dispute; synonyms.

clue.text: Attempt to sell client's foremost old ring

indicators.note: foremost picks the leading letter of the word before it

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone, or call, them

explanation.surface: A salesperson rings the main client, an old customer.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsolicited phone call or visit made to try to sell something; the phrase is a verb too.

clue.text: Oscar, ten, thanks the Italian for soup ingredient?

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
X is the Roman numeral for ten
ta is informal British for thanks
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Seems to list an odd shopping order in a foreign kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-up beef tail is the base of a classic thick soup, so it is an example of an ingredient.

clue.text: Kind offer

definitions.meaning: a formal offer or bid, as for a contract

explanation.definitionFit: Tender means gentle and loving; it also means a formal bid, as in putting work out to tender.

clue.text: Gave to charity, old-fashioned, welcoming cricket side

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: dated means out of fashion
the on side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs, also called leg side

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned club opened its doors to a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: To give money or goods to a cause is to make a gift; synonym.

clue.text: Conflict over the German prison officer

indicators.note: in a down answer over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: war is armed conflict
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A war has ended for a German guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a jailer, a guard who supervises prisoners; synonym.

clue.text: Journey's end, distant one, I recollected

indicators.note: recollected is read as re-collected, gathered again in another order

explanation.surface: A traveller far away remembers how the trip ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered; read it as collected again.
explanation.definitionFit: The place a trip ends is where it was headed; a paraphrase.

clue.text: Smart, regularly visited in silk?

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word before it, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Asks whether a smart regular caller came dressed in silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy fabric often woven from silk, so silk is an example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pressure over fish — appeal to higher power?

indicators.note: in a down answer over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a ray is a flat fish such as a skate

explanation.surface: Seems to be about pressure on a fishery leading to an appeal upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking to God is an appeal to a higher power; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: A non-drinker, one in Paris, with editor, acclimatized

parts.note: TT is teetotal, a non-drinker
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A sober editor in Paris has settled in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean adjusted to fit new surroundings; synonyms.

clue.text: In search of a fine time at school — finishing early

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: Looking for a good spell at school that ended before time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to be seeking it; synonym.

clue.text: Nothing about old floor covering

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing much to say about an old floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for linoleum, a hard floor covering; an example of the category.

clue.text: Amiable lady disheartened by Friday finish

parts.note: end means finish

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman is dispirited by the way her Friday ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves LY from the outside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean warm and well-disposed; synonyms.
